correctness.rationale: Summing F(q)=sum q^j/(j(j+1)) gives 1+(1-q)log(1-q)/q, so V=F(q)-F(q^2). The derivative is H(q)/q^3 and H=q R(q)/(1-q^2)^2 for R(q)=2q^3-q^2-8q+3 with R'(q)=2(q+1)(3q-4)<0. H initially rises, has one local maximum, decreases to -infinity near q=1, hence exactly one positive zero q* at which V is maximized. Since H'(q*)<0, Taylor gives curvature -H'(q*)/(2q*^3)>0. Boundaries q=0 and 1 have V=0; theta fixed in asymptotic limit. Independent check: Independent symbolic differentiation verified identities V'=H/q^3 and H''=qR/(1-q^2)^2, plus high-precision unique-root location, coefficient maximum, fair coin benchmark and quadratic curvature. The bundled source rational-series root bounds were inspected and are finite rational certificates; uniqueness relies on the cubic-monotonicity proof.
